newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Freeport says no impact on mine from tribal clash.
newsitem.headline: Freeport says no impact on mine from tribal clash.

text.p: PT Freeport Indonesia said on Friday a renewed outbreak of tribal violence near the mining town of Timika had had no impact on Freeport's giant copper and gold mine at Tembagapura in remote Irian Jaya province.
"Our operations have not been affected by the latest incident. It was an isolated incident in the lowlands," Freeport Indonesia's Jakarta-based spokesman Ed Pressman told Reuters.

Residents said four people were killed in the clash in the Kwamki Lama area, about about five km (three miles) north of Timika, in a tribal conflict between members of the Amumgne ethnic group on one side and the Dani and Nduga ethnic groups.
No new clashes were reported on Friday and the area was said to be tense but under heavy military guard.

PT Freeport Indonesia, operator of one of the world's largest copper and gold mines at Tembagapura, about 45 km (28 miles) north of Timika, is 81.28 percent owned by Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States.
Indonesian interests own the balance of the firm.
In January, six people were killed and more than 60 injured when thousands of Amungme and Dani tribesman clashed near Tembagapura after an alleged rape.
